Convert MSCZ to PDF

What this does

An .mscz file is a compressed MuseScore score: notation, layout and instrument data, with no PDF inside it. Converting it means running MuseScore's layout engine over the score, which is exactly what this page does — the same engine, compiled to WebAssembly, running in your browser. Page breaks and engraving therefore match what MuseScore shows for that file. The same steps convert a MuseScore file to PDF.

Open the converter with PDF selected

How to convert

  1. Choose a .mscz or .mscx file.
  2. Set the output format to PDF.
  3. Press Convert, then download the PDF.

What you get

One PDF containing the full score as opened: every page, in MuseScore's own pagination. Separate instrumental parts are not split out.

FAQ

Does the PDF match MuseScore's own export?

It comes from the same layout engine, so pagination and engraving match what MuseScore renders for that file.

Can I export separate parts?

No. The output is the full score as opened; export parts in MuseScore itself.

What happens to a font that is not bundled?

The browser build ships only its bundled fonts, so text in an unusual font falls back to a substitute glyph.
